title: Prophecies Against the Prince of Tyre, the King of Tyre, and Sidon

questions.question: What did the prince of Tyre say in the haughtiness of his heart that provoked God's judgment?
options: "I am a god, I sit in the seat of the gods, in the heart of the seas."
"I am the master of the world, greater than Nebuchadnezzar."
"My wealth makes me immortal; my ships touch the heavens."
"I am equal to the God of Israel."
questions.correctAnswer: "I am a god, I sit in the seat of the gods, in the heart of the seas."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:2 (ESV): "Because your heart is proud, and you have said, 'I am a god, I sit in the seat of the gods, in the heart of the seas,'"

questions.question: Despite the prince of Tyre considering himself a god, what does God explicitly say about his true nature?
options: "Yet you are but a man, and no god."
"You are an angel fallen from grace."
"You are a beast of the sea."
"You are dust and to dust you shall return."
questions.correctAnswer: "Yet you are but a man, and no god."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:2 (ESV): "yet you are but a man, and no god, though you make your heart like the heart of a god"

questions.question: In verse 3, the prince of Tyre believes he is wiser than whom?
options: Daniel
Solomon
Enoch
Moses
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:3 (ESV): "you are indeed wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you;"

questions.question: Because the prince made his heart like the heart of a god, who will the Lord bring against him?
options: Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations
The mighty angels of heaven
A great leviathan from the deep
His own mutinous generals
questions.correctAnswer: Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:7 (ESV): "therefore, behold, I will bring foreigners upon you, the most ruthless of the nations;"

questions.question: What penetrating question does God ask the Prince of Tyre about his death?
options: "Will you still say, 'I am a god,' in the presence of those who kill you?"
"Who will sing a lament for you when you fall?"
"Where is your wealth when the sword pierces your heart?"
"Can your ships sail you away from the grave?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Will you still say, 'I am a god,' in the presence of those who kill you?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:9 (ESV): "Will you still say, 'I am a god,' in the presence of those who kill you, though you are but a man, and no god, in the hands of those who slay you?"

questions.question: The second lament in chapter 28 is directed towards the "king of Tyre." In this prophetic lament, where was he placed?
options: In Eden, the garden of God
In Babylon, the great city
In Jerusalem, the holy mountain
In Egypt, the land of the Pharaohs
questions.correctAnswer: In Eden, the garden of God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:13 (ESV): "You were in Eden, the garden of God..." (This passage is heavily debated; many scholars see it pointing past the earthly king to Satan behind the kingdom).

questions.question: What was his covering in Eden?
options: Every precious stone (sardius, topaz, diamond, beryl... etc)
Leaves of the tree of life
Garments of fine purple linen
Scales of pure gold
questions.correctAnswer: Every precious stone (sardius, topaz, diamond, beryl... etc)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:13 (ESV): "every precious stone was your covering, sardius, topaz, and diamond..."

questions.question: What position/role was he placed in on the holy mountain of God?
options: An anointed guardian cherub
The chief of the seraphim
A high priest of the temple
A king over all kings of the earth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:14 (ESV): "I placed you; you were an anointed guardian cherub. You were on the holy mountain of God; in the midst of the stones of fire you walked."

questions.question: How long was he blameless in his ways from the day he was created?
options: Until unrighteousness was found in him
Until he ate the forbidden fruit
Until he saw the beauty of women
Until war broke out in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Until unrighteousness was found in him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:15 (ESV): "You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, till unrighteousness was found in you."

questions.question: In the abundance of his trade, what did he become filled with?
options: Violence
Lust
Greed
Fear
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:16 (ESV): "In the abundance of your trade you were filled with violence in your midst, and you sinned..."

questions.question: Because his heart was proud of his beauty, he corrupted his wisdom for the sake of his splendor. What was his punishment?
options: He was cast to the ground and exposed before kings to feast their eyes on him
He was chained in darkness for a thousand years
He was turned into a serpent
He was stripped of his wings forever
questions.correctAnswer: He was cast to the ground and exposed before kings to feast their eyes on him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:17 (ESV): "Your heart was proud because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. I cast you to the ground; I exposed you before kings, to feast their eyes on you."

questions.question: What did God make come out from his midst, consuming him to ashes on the earth?
options: Fire
A sword
Water
A plague
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:18 (ESV): "therefore I brought fire out from your midst; it consumed you, and I turned you to ashes on the earth..."

questions.question: After Tyre, who does Ezekiel prophesy against next in chapter 28?
options: Sidon
Jerusalem
Damascus
Gaza
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:21 (ESV): "Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against her"

questions.question: God says concerning Sidon, "And for the house of Israel there shall be no more a brier to prick or a... to hurt them among all their neighbors"
options: Thorn
Lions
Whip
Scorpion
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:24 (ESV): "And for the house of Israel there shall be no more a brier to prick or a thorn to hurt them among all their neighbors who have treated them with contempt..."

questions.question: What is the promise to the house of Israel at the very end of chapter 28?
options: They shall dwell securely in their land that I gave to my servant Jacob
They shall conquer the seas and build ships like Tyre
They shall reign over the king of Babylon
They will discover gold in the mountains of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: They shall dwell securely in their land that I gave to my servant Jacob
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:25-26 (ESV): "...and they shall dwell securely. They shall build houses and plant vineyards... when I execute judgments upon all their neighbors... Then they will know that I am the Lord their God."

key_verse_text: "Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre, Thus says the Lord God: Because your heart is proud, and you have said, 'I am a god, I sit in the seat of the gods, in the heart of the seas,' yet you are but a man, and no god, though you make your heart like the heart of a god—"
